newsitem.title: USA: ST. MARY LAND EXPLORATION RESULTS EXCELLENT.
newsitem.headline: ST. MARY LAND EXPLORATION RESULTS EXCELLENT.

text.p: St. Mary Land & Exploration Co said on Thursday its 1997 exploration and development results to-date are excellent.
"Third quarter production will reflect a series of significant completions stemming from active drilling programs in our core areas," chief executive Mark Hellerstein said.
Average daily domestic oil and gas production during the second quarter was 13,157 barrels of oil equivalent, up from 10,022 barrels a year earlier, the company said.

"We presently are operating six drilling rigs and expect to operate a record total of approximately 50 wells in 1997, a 100 percent increase over the 25 wells operated by the company in 1996," Hellerstein said. "In addition, we should participate during the year in an additional 60 to 75 wells operated by others."
The company said the St. Mary Land and Exploration No. 3 offset to the February 1997 discovery at South Horseshoe Bayou was started on August 3 by the operator, Mobil Corp.
St. Mary said this offset well is designed to produce the uppermost 17,300 foot pay zone near the structure's crest.
This would enable the existing No. 2 well to be recompleted in a lower pay zone at about 17,900 feet.
St. Mary holds a 40 percent net revenue interest in both wells. A spokesman said unitization of the tract has been approved, but working interests in the unit have not been set.

The company said the initial test of its block in the shallow waters of Atchafalaya Bay is scheduled to start in late August, pending final permits, using a barge-mounted drilling rig. St. Mary holds a 40 percent working interest in this 3-D defined structure.

The company said a lease of its Bell Bayou Prospect fee lands has been finalized and the first of three prospects is expected to start drilling by year-end. St. Mary retains a 25 percent royalty interest and has the option to participate for up to a 25 percent working interest. In addition, St. Mary will receive a lease bonus payment of about $500,000.

It said the Carter Estate 1 discovery at the Roanoke Prospect in Jefferson Davis Parish is expected to start production in late August following completion of a pipeline connection which had been delayed pending receipt of necessary rights of way. St. Mary has a 33.3 percent working interest.
The company said it plans to operate four drilling rigs in the Mid-Continent region throughout the balance of 1997.

The $26.5 million Mid-Continent program is divided between lower-risk Granite Wash wells targeting potential reserves of 1.5 to three billion cubic feet per well where St. Mary had a 94 percent success rate in 1995 and 1996; Red Fork tests targeting potential reserves of between three and five billion cubic feet per well; and higher-risk deep Morrow tests targeting reserves of between five and 30 billion cubic feet per well.
In the Mid-Continent region through July, 40 wells have been drilled or recompleted with a 92 percent success rate; an additional 8 wells are awaiting completion; and 10 wells are presently drilling.

At the Box Church Field in east Texas the company-operated 1997-1998 development program is proceeding on schedule. St. Mary has an average working interest of 58 percent in gross field production now exceeding 27 million cubic feet daily.
